references.text: Moses went out to his brothers the day before, which establishes the context for this second day when he goes out again.
The command to rebuke one's neighbor and not bear sin against him, as Moses does when he confronts the man who strikes his fellow countryman.
Stephen refers directly to this event in his speech, where Moses tries to reconcile two Israelites who are fighting.
The proverb about leaving a quarrel before it breaks out, relevant to the conflict between the two Hebrews.
Abram asks that there be no strife between brothers, a similar theme of conflict among countrymen.
Violence and strife in the city, thematically parallel to the dispute Moses witnesses.
